Rashi on Pesachim 29a:10:1.hebrew: את יוה"כ כשבת - המדליק גדיש ביוה"כ, ומתחייב כרת, פטור מן התשלומין — כאילו הדליקו בשבת, שהוא מתחייב בנפשו מיתת ב"ד, דפשיטא לן דפטור מלשלם, כדכתיב (שמות כ״א:כ״ב): ״ולא יהיה אסון ענוש יענש״ — הא אם אסון יהיה, לא יענש; שאף יוה"כ, שמיתתו בידי שמים שנכרתים חייו ובניו, ״אסון״ הוא קרוי, שנא' (בראשית מ״ב:ל״ח): ״וקרהו אסון״; הלכך, פטור מלשלם. והכי פרשינן לה ב״אלו נערות״. יש טועים דקשיא להו: כי פטר ר' נחוניא — במזיד פטר, דבר כרת הוא, והכא בשוגג עסקינן, מדקתני ״מעל״, ושוגג לאו בר כרת הוא?! וטעות הוא זה: דגבי חמץ מזיד הוא, וגבי הקדש שוגג הוא, דלא ידע שהוא של הקדש:
Rashi on Pesachim 29a:10:1.english: Yom Kippur like Shabbat - One who sets fire to a stack of grain on Yom Kippur and thereby incurs karet is exempt from payment, just as if he had set fire to it on Shabbat, where he incurs [liability for] his life with court-imposed execution, for which it is obvious to us that he is exempt from paying, as it is written: (Exodus 21:22) “And if no harm follow, he shall surely be fined” — implying: but if harm follow, he shall not be fined; for even Yom Kippur, whose death [penalty] is by the hand of Heaven, in that his life and his children are cut off, is termed “harm,” as it is stated: (Genesis 42:38) “Lest harm befall him”; therefore, he is exempt from paying. And this is how we explained it in [the chapter entitled] “Elu Na’arot.” There are those who err, to whom it is difficult: When Rabbi Neḥunya exempted [an offender], he exempted [him] in an intentional case, which is a matter of karet; whereas here we are dealing with an unintentional case, since it teaches that he committed misuse [of consecrated property], and an unintentional [offender] is not subject to karet! But this is an error, for regarding leaven he is an intentional [offender], and regarding consecrated property he is an unintentional [offender], as he did not know that it belonged to consecrated property.

Rashi on Pesachim 29a:12:1.hebrew: ורב יוסף אמר - אי הוה סבירא להנך תנאי כרבי שמעון, דאמר תוך זמנו אסור בהנאה — דכולי עלמא מודו דפטור, הואיל והשתא מיהא לא חזי ולאו ממונא הוא, ואע"ג דסופו גורם הוא לממון לאחר הפסח. אלא אליבא דר' יוסי הגלילי פליגי, דאמר תוך זמנו נמי שרי בהנאה, ובפודין קדשים להאכילן לכלבים קא מיפלגי: מאן דאמר מעל סבר, דראוי היה באותה שעה לפדות לאכילת כלבים ובר דמים הוא, ודר' נחוניא לית ליה:
Rashi on Pesachim 29a:12:1.english: And Rav Yosef said - If these Tanna’im held in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, who said [that leaven] during its time is forbidden for benefit, everyone would agree that he is exempt, since for now at least it is not fit [for use] and is not property, even though it ultimately causes monetary value after Passover. Rather, they disagree according to [the opinion of] Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, who said [that] during its time it is also permitted for benefit; and they disagree over [whether] one may redeem consecrated items in order to feed them to dogs: The one who says [that] he committed misuse holds that at that time it was fit to be redeemed for feeding to dogs and has monetary value; and he does not hold [in accordance with the opinion of] Rabbi Neḥunya.

Rashi on Pesachim 29a:13:1.hebrew: ומאן דאמר לא מעל סבר אין פודין - הלכך לא חזי. ופלוגתא דתנאי היא בתמורה (דף לא.): "תזבח" — ולא גיזה, "בשר" — ולא חלב, "ואכלת" — ולא לכלבים, מכאן שאין פודין. ואיכא דדריש: "תזבח ואכלת" — אין לך בהן היתר אכילה אלא לאחר זביחה, למעוטי גיזה וחלב; אבל "לא לכלביך" לא דריש:
Rashi on Pesachim 29a:13:1.english: And the one who said that he did not misuse [consecrated items] holds that one may not redeem - Therefore, [the consecrated leaven] is not fit [for any use]. And it is a dispute of Tannaim in Temurah (daf 31a): "You shall slaughter" — but not shear [its wool]; "meat" — but not [consume its] milk; "and you shall eat" — but not [feed it] to dogs; from here [it is derived] that one may not redeem [consecrated items to feed them to dogs]. And there is [a Tanna] who expounds: "You shall slaughter and eat" — you have permission to eat of them only after slaughter, [which comes] to exclude shearing and milk; but "not for your dogs" he does not expound.

Rashi on Pesachim 29a:1:1.english: That of a Jew, he also permits - For benefit, after its time.

Rashi on Pesachim 29a:2:1.hebrew: לעולם ר' יהודה היא - דאע"ג דנפקא ליה מקראי דלאחר זמנו אסר, קרא בשאור דישראל קאמר, אבל דנכרי שרי:
Rashi on Pesachim 29a:2:1.english: Actually, it is [in accordance with] Rabbi Yehuda - For even though he derives from verses that [the Torah] forbade [chametz] after its time, the verse is speaking of the leaven of an Israelite, but that of a gentile is permitted.

Rashi on Pesachim 29a:2:2.hebrew: ויליף שאור דאכילה - כלומר, חמץ דגבי לא יאכל משאור דראייה, ומותר חמצו של נכרי אף באכילה, ואפי' בפסח מן התורה:
Rashi on Pesachim 29a:2:2.english: And he derives the leaven of eating - That is to say, [he derives the prohibition of] leaven regarding "it shall not be eaten" from the leaven of seeing; and the leaven of a gentile is permitted even for eating, and even on Passover, by Torah law.

Rashi on Pesachim 29a:4:1.hebrew: לעולם ר' שמעון היא - דאמר: מדאורייתא לא מיתסר חמץ אחר זמנו, הלכך דנכרי שרי. ומיהו, דישראל אסור מקנסא דקנסוהו רבנן, משום דעבר בבל יראה:
Rashi on Pesachim 29a:4:1.english: Actually, it is [in accordance with] Rabbi Shimon - For he says [that] by Torah law, chametz after its time is not forbidden; therefore, that of a gentile is permitted. However, that of a Jew is forbidden due to a penalty that the Sages penalized him, because he transgressed [the prohibition of] “it shall not be seen.”

Rashi on Pesachim 29a:5:1.hebrew: בשלמא לרבא - דאמר טעמא דאסור בהנאה משום קנסא דעבר בבל יראה הוא — היינו דתנא מתני': "אסור משום לא יראה לך":
Rashi on Pesachim 29a:5:1.english: Granted, according to Rava - For he said [that] the reason it is forbidden to derive benefit [from it] is as a penalty, because he transgressed [the prohibition of] "it shall not be seen" — that is why the Mishnah taught: "[It is] forbidden because [it is stated]: 'There shall not be seen to you'."

Rashi on Pesachim 29a:7:1.english: And they follow their line of reasoning - Rava and Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov.

Rashi on Pesachim 29a:9:1.hebrew: מעל - חייב קרבן מעילה, דקסבר: חמץ דהקדש בפסח בר דמים הוא, ואפסדיה להקדש, כר' שמעון, דאמר חמץ לאחר הפסח מותר. ואע"ג דקנסא קניס — ה"מ בחמצו של הדיוט, הואיל ועבר עליו בבל יראה; אבל האי, דבהתירא שהייה גביה — דאמר מר (לעיל פסחים דף ה:): "אבל אתה רואה של אחרים ושל גבוה" — אחר הפסח הוה מזבין ליה גיזבר לישראל, ואכלי ליה:
Rashi on Pesachim 29a:9:1.english: Is guilty of misuse - He is liable [to bring] a guilt-offering for misuse, for [the Tanna] holds that consecrated chametz on Passover has monetary value, and he caused a loss to the sanctuary, in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, who says [that] chametz after Passover is permitted. And even though [Rabbi Shimon] penalizes [one who keeps chametz], this applies only to the chametz of an ordinary person, since he violated [the prohibition of] "it shall not be seen" regarding it; but this [consecrated chametz], which [the treasurer] kept in his possession permissibly — as the Master said (above, Pesachim 5b): "But you may see [chametz] belonging to others and belonging to the Most High" — after Passover the treasurer would sell it to an Israelite and they would eat it.

Rashi on Pesachim 29a:9:2.hebrew: ויש אומרים לא מעל - כדמפרש, דהואיל ונתחייב כרת משום אכילה — פטור מן התשלומין, כר' נחוניא; ובמקום שאין קרן, אין חומש ואין מעילה:
Rashi on Pesachim 29a:9:2.english: And some say: He is not guilty of misuse - As [the Gemara] explains: Since he incurred karet for eating [it], he is exempt from [monetary] restitution, in accordance with Rabbi Neḥunya; and wherever there is no principal, there is no [added] fifth and no [liability for] misuse.

Tosafot on Pesachim 29a:10:1.hebrew: מאן יש אומרים ר' נחוניא - תימה לר"י: דמאן דיליף "אסון" "אסון" בריש אלו נערו' (כתובות ל.), ואית ליה מיתה בידי שמים פטור מן התשלומים לר' נחוניא — אם כן לרבי, דאמר לקמן (פסחים דף לג.) "הזיד במעילה במיתה", אמאי פוטר כרת מתשלומים? והא אע"ג דבעלמא פוטר מיתה מתשלומין, הכא לא פטר — דגלי לן קרא דבשוגג חייב; וה"ה כרת, אע"ג דבכרת הוא במזיד, בשוגג יתחייב! ואור"י: דבמיתה דגלי לן קרא דלא פטרה הכא מתשלומים — גלי; בכרת דלא גלי — לא גלי. וא"ת: והא אמר לקמן (פסחים דף לא:) "האוכל תרומת חמץ בפסח בשוגג משלם קרן וחומש", ומוקמי' לה כר' נחוניא, ואפ"ה מיחייב בתשלומין — משום דכי היכי דלא מיפטר מתשלומין משום חיוב מיתה דתרומה, הכי נמי לא מיפטר משום כרת של חמץ? ואור"י: דתשלומי תרומה מחמת כפרה הם, כדמוכח במסכת תרומות (פ"ו מ"א), דתנן: "אם רצה כהן למחול אינו יכול למחול"; וכיון דכפרה הוא, אין כרת פוטרו משום "קם ליה בדרבה מיניה". ותדע: דהא מאן דלא יליף "אסון" "אסון", ולא פטר מיתה בידי שמים מתשלומין — אם כן, אוכל תרומת חמץ אמאי משלם? דלא שייך למימר 'כיון שמיתה אינה פוטרת ה"ה כרת', דהא מיתה לא פטרה בשום מקום; אלא ע"כ מטעם כפרה הוא. ועוד אור"י: דהכא אתי אליבא דרבנן, דאמרי: הזיד במעילה באזהרה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 29a:10:1.english: Who is "some say"? Rabbi Neḥunya - [This is] astonishing to the Ri: For according to the one who derives [via the verbal analogy of] ason [and] ason in the beginning of [the chapter entitled] Elu Na'arot (Ketubot 30a), and holds that [according to Rabbi Neḥunya, even one liable to] death at the hands of Heaven is exempt from payment — if so, according to Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], who says later (Pesachim 33a) [that one who] intentionally committed misuse [of consecrated property is punished] by death [at the hands of Heaven], why does karet exempt [him] from payment? For even though elsewhere [under Rabbi Neḥunya's view] death [at the hands of Heaven] exempts from payment, here [concerning misuse of consecrated property] it does not exempt, since the verse revealed to us that [if committed] unwittingly he is liable [to pay the principal and a fifth]; and the same should apply to karet: even though [eating leaven] intentionally carries karet, unwittingly he should be liable [to pay for misuse]! And the Ri says: Concerning death [at the hands of Heaven], where the verse revealed to us that it does not exempt here from payment, it revealed [it]; but concerning karet, where it did not reveal, it did not reveal. And if you say: But doesn't [the Gemara] say later (Pesachim 31b): "One who unwittingly eats terumah of leaven on Passover pays the principal and a fifth," and we establish it in accordance with Rabbi Neḥunya, and even so he is liable for payment — because just as he is not exempt from payment on account of the liability of death [at the hands of Heaven] for terumah, so too he is not exempt on account of the karet of leaven?! And the Ri says: Payments for terumah are on account of atonement, as is proven in tractate Terumot (6:1), where we learned: "If the priest wished to forgive [the payment], he cannot forgive [it]"; and since it is [for] atonement, karet does not exempt him due to [the principle of] "he receives the greater [punishment]" (kam lei bid'rabba minei). And know [that this is so]: for according to the one who does not derive ason [and] ason, and [therefore] does not exempt [one liable to] death at the hands of Heaven from payment — if so, why does one who eats terumah of leaven pay? For it is not applicable to say "since death does not exempt, the same applies to karet," as death does not exempt anywhere [according to him]; rather, it is perforce on account of atonement. And furthermore, the Ri says: Here [in our sugya], it proceeds according to the Rabbis, who say: [One who] intentionally committed misuse [of consecrated property is subject only to] a negative prohibition.

Tosafot on Pesachim 29a:10:2.hebrew: רבי נחוניא היא - אע"ג דהכא בשוגג איירי, מדקתני: "מעל ולא מעל" — מ"מ קיימא לן כחזקיה, דאמר: "חייבי מיתות שוגגין פטורים מן התשלומין", וה"ה כרת לר' נחוניא. הקשה ריב"א: אמאי פטורין הכא מקרבן מעילה משום ד"קם ליה בדרבה מיניה"? הא אמר בהמצניע (שבת צד:): המוציא אוכלים בכלי, שגג באוכלים והזיד בכלי — חייב על האוכלים חטאת ועל הכלי סקילה; אלמא "קם ליה בדרבה מיניה" לא פטר מקרבן! ותירץ: כיון דפטר מקרן וחומש — פטר נמי מקרבן, שאין אשם מעילות בא אלא כשיש קרן וחומש:
Tosafot on Pesachim 29a:10:2.english: "It is Rabbi Neḥunya" - Even though here it is dealing with [an act performed] unwittingly, since it teaches: "He committed misuse" and "he did not commit misuse"; nevertheless, we maintain in accordance with Ḥizkiya, who said: "Those liable to execution [who acted] unwittingly are exempt from payment," and the same applies to karet according to Rabbi Neḥunya. The Riva asked: Why are they exempt here from a sacrifice for misuse on account of [the principle of] "he receives the greater [punishment]" (kam lei bid'rabba minei)? But didn't [the Gemara] say in [the chapter entitled] HaMatznia (Shabbat 94b): "One who carries out food in a vessel [on Shabbat], if he acted unwittingly regarding the food and intentionally regarding the vessel, he is liable [to bring] a sin-offering for the food and [to suffer] stoning for the vessel"! Thus, "he receives the greater [punishment]" does not exempt [one] from a sacrifice! And he answered: Since he is exempt from the principal and the [added] fifth, he is also exempt from the sacrifice, for a guilt-offering for misuse is brought only when there is [liability for] principal and a fifth.

Tosafot on Pesachim 29a:13:1.hebrew: אין פודין את הקדשים וכו' - הקשה הר"ח: דבפ"ב דבכורות (דף יד:) משמע דלא פליגי אלא היכא שקדם הקדישן למומן, אבל קדם מומן להקדישן — הואיל ומעולם לא קדשו קדושת הגוף, כ"ע מודים דפודים; והכא משמע דפליגי אפי' בקדושת דמים! ותי' ר"י: דה"ק — אין פודין מדרבנן. ואין לתמוה: אטו משום חששא דרבנן נפקיע מעילה דאורייתא? דכיון דאמרו רבנן "אין פודין" — לא שויא מידי. והא דאמר בהתערובות (זבחים עא.): "נתערבו בשור שנעבדה וכו' בכלאים וטריפה — ירעו עד שיסתאבו וימכרו", והשתא ע"כ יאכיל לכלבים, דלישראל טריפה אסורה ליה — אתי שפיר אפילו למאן דאמר "אין פודין"; דהא דאין פודין היינו היכא דלא חזו לאכילה, אבל הכא חזו לאדם אם היו ניכרים. דהא רבי עקיבא שרי בבכורות (דף לב.) לזמן נכרי על הבכור, ובזבחים בפ' טבול יום (זבחים דף קד.) מוכח שר' עקיבא אוסר בכור טריפה בעל מום להאכיל לכלבים, שאפילו העור אסור כשנמצא טריפה קודם הפשט, והיכא דשרי לישראל — איתקש לצבי ולאיל:
Tosafot on Pesachim 29a:13:1.english: "One may not redeem consecrated items, etc." - Rabbeinu Chananel raised a difficulty: For in the second chapter of Bekhorot (14b), it implies that they disagree only where their consecration preceded their blemish; but if their blemish preceded their consecration, since they were never consecrated with physical sanctity, everyone agrees that one may redeem [them to feed them to dogs]. Yet here, it implies that they disagree even regarding monetary sanctity! And Ri answered that this is what it means: One may not redeem [consecrated items to feed them to dogs] by Rabbinic decree. And one should not wonder: Would we, on account of a Rabbinic concern, eliminate [the Torah prohibition of] misuse of consecrated items? For since the Rabbis said, "One may not redeem," it is not worth anything. And that which [the Mishnah] states in [the chapter entitled] Hata'arovot (Zevachim 71a) — [that if sacrificial animals] became mixed with an ox with which a transgression was committed, etc., with a crossbred animal, or with a tereifah, "they shall graze until they develop a blemish and be sold," and now [the purchaser] perforce will feed [the tereifah] to dogs, since for an Israelite a tereifah is forbidden to him [to eat] — works out well even according to the one who says, "One may not redeem." For that which [he holds that] one may not redeem applies only where they are not fit for [human] consumption; but here, they would be fit for a person if they were identifiable. For Rabbi Akiva permits in Bekhorot (32a) inviting a gentile to [eat of] a firstborn, and in Zevachim in the chapter [entitled] Tevul Yom (104a), it is proven that Rabbi Akiva forbids feeding a blemished firstborn that is a tereifah to dogs, for even the hide is forbidden when it is found to be a tereifah prior to flaying; and [only] where it is permitted to an Israelite was it equated to a gazelle and a deer.

Tosafot on Pesachim 29a:13:2.hebrew: אין פודין - תימה לר"י: אע"ג דאין פודין, נמעול, דהא לאחר שנשרף ונעשה אפר יכול לפדותו, ומותר בהנאה! ויש לומר: דכיון דכמו שהוא עכשיו לא שוי מידי, לא שייכא ביה מעילה. והיינו נמי טעמא דכל איסורי הנאה אין מקדשין בהן האשה, אע"ג דכל הנשרפין אפרן מותר. ואפילו אי "דבר הגורם לממון כממון דמי" ומעל — לא דמי, דהתם חזי לאחר הפסח, שהוא כמו בעין. ועוד יש לומר: הא דאין מקדשין באיסורי הנאה — היינו היכא דלית ביה שוה פרוטה לכשיהא אפר. ולתירוץ קמא קשה: הא חזי בעיניה שלא כדרך הנאה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 29a:13:2.english: One may not redeem: [This is] astonishing to the Ri: Even though one may not redeem [consecrated items to feed them to dogs], let him be liable for misuse [of consecrated property], for after it is burned and becomes ash, one can redeem it, and it is permitted for benefit! And one can say: Since as it is right now it is not worth anything, misuse [of consecrated property] does not apply to it. And this is also the reason that with all items forbidden for benefit, one cannot betroth a woman with them, even though anything that is [to be] burned, its ashes are permitted [for benefit]. And even if [one holds that] "something that causes monetary value is treated as money" and [therefore] he would be liable for misuse — it is not comparable; for there, it is usable after Passover while it is [still] intact [be'ayin]. And furthermore, one can say: That which they do not betroth [a woman] with items forbidden for benefit is [only] where it does not contain the value of a perutah once it becomes ash. And against the first answer, it is difficult: but it is usable in its actual state in an abnormal manner of benefit!

Tosafot on Pesachim 29a:3:1.hebrew: בדין הוא דאפי' תוך זמנו מותר - פרש"י: מותר באכילה. וקשה, דאי אפשר אם לא יהא שלו בשעת אכילה: דאם נתן לו הנכרי — הרי הוא שלו, ואם גזל מנכרי — הרי חייב באחריותו, ולא גרע מחמץ שחייב באחריותו דהוי כשלו! ועוד, לקמן דקאמר: "ואזדו לטעמייהו, דפליגי בחמץ שעבר עליו הפסח — ליפלגו בפסח גופיה!" ונראה לריב"א, דהא דקאמר "אפי' תוך זמנו מותר" — היינו בהנאה; והא דקאמר "אבל אתה אוכל של אחרים" — לאו דוקא; אי נמי, אחר זמנו קאמר. ומיהו, בשל גבוה קשה לפרש בתוך הפסח: דאם לא פדאו — אסור בהנאה, ואם פדאו — הרי הוא שלו! ושמא י"ל: "אבל אתה נהנה משל גבוה" — שלא יהא איסור חמץ, אבל איסור הקדש יש:
Tosafot on Pesachim 29a:3:1.english: "By right, even during its time it is permitted" - Rashi explained [that this means it is] permitted for eating. And this is difficult, for it is impossible [to eat it] without it being his at the time of eating: For if the gentile gave it to him, it is [now] his; and if he stole it from a gentile, he bears liability for it, and it is no worse than chametz for which one bears financial responsibility, which is considered like his own! And furthermore, later on [29b] where [the Gemara] says: "And they follow their own reasoning, for where they disagree is regarding chametz after Passover has passed; let them disagree regarding Passover itself!" And it appears to the Riva that that which [the Gemara] says, "even during its time it is permitted," means [permitted] for benefit; and that which [the Gemara] says, "but you may eat [the leaven] of others," was not exact; alternatively, he was speaking of after its time. However, regarding [chametz] belonging to the Sanctuary, it is difficult to explain [that this applies] during Passover: for if he did not redeem it, it is forbidden to derive benefit [from it due to me'ilah], and if he did redeem it, it is his! And perhaps one can say: "but you may derive benefit from that belonging to the Sanctuary" — [means] that there is no prohibition of chametz, but a prohibition of consecrated property [still] applies.
